why: Measured on 2026-09-17 on `mastra-ai/mastra` (husky `^9.1.7`): rebar printed `hooks-executable ✗ … .husky/pre-commit — fix with: git update-index --chmod=+x`, about a hook that runs there on every commit, and following the advice would have changed nothing. Read from the published `husky@9.1.7` tarball: `index.js` runs `git config core.hooksPath .husky/_`, writes `.husky/_/<hook>` ITSELF with `mode: 0o755`, copies its `husky` script to `.husky/_/h`, and writes `.husky/_/.gitignore` as `*` so none of that is committed; `.husky/_/h` ends with `sh -e "$s" "$@"`, where `$s` is the committed `.husky/<hook>`. It is sourced through an explicit interpreter, so the execute bit on the committed file decides nothing, and husky 9 hooks carry no shebang by design. THE VERSION IS THE WHOLE OF THE DIFFERENCE, and it is what the two sides here differ in: `husky@8.0.3` (`lib/index.js`, read the same way) runs `git config core.hooksPath <dir>` with `<dir>` being `.husky` ITSELF, the committed directory — there git executes the committed file directly and a 100644 hook is ignored on Linux exactly as the rule says. The two trees are the same bytes, the same 100644 mode and the same `.husky/pre-commit`; only the declared major changes. Whoever exempts on the PATH — `.husky/` and husky in the manifest, with no version — turns the fail side green and stops accusing every husky 8 repository there is.
